title: The Addiction to Being Right
topic: Why traders would rather prove themselves right than protect their capital.

scenes.title: The addiction to being right
scenes.subtitle: Why traders would rather be right than protect their capital
scenes.voiceover: Most traders aren't addicted to money. They're addicted to being right.
You enter a trade. It moves against you. Price slices through your stop, and you do nothing.
Your stop says get out. Your ego says it'll come back. So you move the stop, and you hope.

scenes.headline: The math doesn't care about your ego
scenes.footer: Every “it'll come back” digs the hole deeper.
scenes.voiceover: Lose ten percent, you need eleven to recover. Lose half, and you need to double your account.

lines.text: Being right feels like a reward.
Taking a loss feels like defeat.
So you protect your ego, and sacrifice your account.

scenes.voiceover: Being right feels like a reward. Taking a loss feels like defeat. So you protect your ego, and sacrifice your account.

scenes.headline: The fix
items: Set your stop before you enter
A small loss is a good trade
scenes.voiceover: Set your stop before you enter. Never move it further away. And remember, a small loss is a good trade.

scenes.lead: The market doesn't pay you for being right.
scenes.voiceover: The market doesn't pay you for being right. It pays you for surviving.
